title: Quick quant + eval scratch journal
content:
Context / goal:
- Trying to squeeze 13B model into an int8-ish profile without egregious quality regressions for our low-latency chat route. Fast experiment log for morning run.

Quick todo (today):
- [ ] run int8 static + per-channel test with new kernel flags on a single A100-80GB 
- [ ] produce quality sweep on 150 prompt seeds (mix dialog + code + factual)
- [ ] push select calibration bits to /mnt/benchstore/devin/quant_runs/2026-03-16
- [ ] share short summary in #aml-kv with Anya before EOD

Run notes (lightweight):
- experiment id: dev-2026-03-16-q8-lite
- model: rw-13b-v2 (fp16 baseline)
- quant configs tried (today):
  * ql8-static-channelwise (per-channel symmetric, outlier clip 0.02)
  * ql4-hybrid (embedding linear int8, attention int4 packed)
  * ql8-dynamic (runtime per-batch scaling)

Commands used (copyable):
- python tools/quantize.py --model rw-13b-v2 --format channelwise --clip 0.02 --out /mnt/benchstore/devin/q8-static
- python -m bench.run_eval --model /mnt/benchstore/devin/q8-static --prompts prompts/seedset-150.json --batch 8 --kv-cache on --stream false --out results/q8-static-seedset-150.json

First-pass observations:
- ql8-static: latency ~ +8% compared to fp16 baseline at seq=512, tokens/sec drop modest. RNG: stable. Quality: rouge-like proxy shows -1.6 points on avg (worst for code prompts). Errors: occasional tokenization mismatch for code fences -> look into prompt tokenization preproc.
- ql4-hybrid: latency improved (tokens/sec +14%) but hallucination rate up ~5% on factual QA prompts. Embedding-space drift noticeable in semantic-sim similarity checks (embedding cosine down ~0.03).
- ql8-dynamic: promising latency but occasional spikes to baseline latency due to runtime scale computation; needs warm cache.

Quick table (throughput vs quality proxy):
- fp16 baseline | tps 420 | proxy-score 0.00 (ref)
- ql8-static    | tps 385 | proxy-score -1.6
- ql4-hybrid    | tps 480 | proxy-score -3.2
- ql8-dynamic   | tps 410 | proxy-score -1.1 (but unstable)

Things to try next (hypotheses):
- tune clipping threshold per-layer (smaller for MLP layers seemed to help in older runs)
- try per-channel + residual compensation (low-cost correction term)
- enable kv-cache prefix reuse across eval batch to amortize dynamic scaling cost
- run targeted eval on 40 code prompts isolated to reproduce tokenization mismatch

Prompt-level failure notes (examples):
- prompt id P_092: "Explain the bug in the following Rust code..." -> ql8-static returned truncated wrap at closing brace. Suspect length computation bug when tokenized tokens cross chunk boundary in quantized runtime.
- prompt id C_014: code generation fine but variable names randomized (consistent token substitution) under ql4-hybrid -> embedding collision?

Data & artifacts layout (local):
- /mnt/benchstore/devin/quant_runs/2026-03-16/
  * q8-static/ (model artifacts, quant metadata file: quant_meta.json)
  * q4-hybrid/
  * eval-results/ (jsonl per-prompt)
  * logs/ (bench logs + perf counters)

Perf counters worth checking in next run:
- memcpy hotspots during attention kernel (observed 12% time in memcpy in last prof run)
- per-layer GEMM throughput variance (layer 18 + 21 worse)
- allocator fragmentation (small peaks during dynamic quant path)

Short checklist before sharing with Anya:
- [ ] re-run ql8-static with explicit tokenize->validate step for code fences
- [ ] snapshot perf counters and attach to PR 789
- [ ] include 6 representative prompts (2 dialog, 2 code, 2 factual) and attach outputs

Notes-to-self (random):
- remember: when benchmarking small batch sizes, the startup jitter matters — run 3 warmup runs and drop first result.
- we have older notes on per-channel clip heuristic in /confluence/aml/quant/hints (need link) — check them if clip tuning weird.
- if ql4-hybrid keeps causing embedding drift, try running a short fine-tune calibration pass on a small LM-adapter, but low priority.

Questions / unresolved:
- is runtime fallback to fp16 happening silently for attention on some kernels? (need trace flag)
- should we add a small stochastic rounding step to hybrid path to reduce deterministic collisions?

Slack snippets to post (draft):
- "Morning: quick quant sketch — ql8-static looks closest to baseline with small perf hit (-1.6 quality proxy). ql4-hybrid faster but more hallucinations; running code-targeted repros. Will share artifacts in benchstore and short note by 5pm. — Devin"

References / links I want to copy into the ticket:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789
- Linear: https://linear.app/REDWOOD/issue/RED-4123
- Benchmark seedset: https://drive.redwood.ai/prompts/seedset-150.json

- [2026-03-16 09:03:02] bench.run_eval: batch=8 seq=512 gpu=0 tps=387 latency_p50=12.4ms

End notes: keep this lightweight. Will formalize into a proper bench doc if one of the configs looks good for a canary rollout.
